_note: Short overviews for lore concepts that only had a quoted in-game mention. Written from the Fandom wiki and the datamine game text; they replace 'excerpt' summaries only, never reviewed ones (concept_summaries.json).
Ancient Civilization: An umbrella term for the lost civilisations whose ruins and frequency traces turn up across Solaris-3, at sites such as Whining Aix's Mire. How they relate to the Pre-Lament Civilization and to Rover's homeland is left open, and fan theories lean on them heavily.
Awakening: The moment someone becomes a Resonator: their Resonance Ability manifests and a Tacet Mark appears. Resonance Evaluation Reports log when, and if known why, a Resonator awakened; a later Secondary Resonance Awakening can deepen it, as with Jinhsi and the Temporal Mandate.
Civilization Capsule: A Sentinel's store of legacy data. In Rinascita one surfaces carrying Imperator's legacy and opens when Rover touches Avidius, pulling them inside; Hsin remolded Mengzhou's while building Xuanfang Hold.
Dollmaker: A criminal of the Séance Society, schooled in the mechanist arts of the Zhuojun Atelier, who makes lifelike dolls. Yinlin's investigation in Jinzhou follows his trail.
Duskveil: The Duskveil Plan: an Antivoid Canopy, a Voidmatter barrier meant to seal Startorch Academy, Lahai-Roi and the Dimmr Plains below it, containing Aleph-1's attack to protect the rest of Solaris.
Ebony Gatekeeper: The black-cat warden of the Somnoire. With the Ivory Gatekeeper it guards the dream realm's gateway and regulates it under the authority of Meta, the Somnoire's mysterious owner.
Ivory Gatekeeper: The white-cat counterpart of the Ebony Gatekeeper. Together they guard the Somnoire's gateway and keep the dream realm in order under its owner, Meta.
Enlightened One: The title of the Resonator chosen by Rinascita's Sentinel, Imperator, foretold by the Order of the Deep. Primus Fenrico claimed it, and Ragunna credits him with surviving the Dark Tide twenty years ago.
Fleurdelys: The Blessed Maiden of the Order of the Deep, revered as a saint and the vessel of Imperator's divinity, remembered for quelling the second Dark Tide by martyrdom. It was Cartethyia's holy name; the two were later split and remerged.
Geshu Lin: A Huanglong official brought down by Jinzhou's Threnodian. Mingting's Censorate ordered Qiuyuan to kill him, but Qiuyuan spared him, seeing he had not yet fallen to darkness; his case later becomes the key to Qiuyuan's own.
Haultir: The Sword of Virtue, bestowed on the Blessed Maiden at a sacred trial site in Rinascita and raised by her when knighting a squire.
Hero of Heroes: Septimont's prophesied champion. Tales of past heroes such as Fabius, Atilius and Valeria fill its histories; Avidius was tipped as the next, while Rover sees Augusta as the one 'rising from the dark tides'.
High Tide: The seasons when the Dark Tide surges around Septimont. Gladiators from across the city-state come to hunt its creations for glory.
Hyvatia: The Hyvatia Detector, a critical sensor for Lahai-Roi's Reactor Drive. It malfunctioned during calibration and injured Professor Mornye; a planted device turned out to be the cause.
Korlacchi: A knightly ideal from Rinascita's old tales; townsfolk speak admiringly of the 'knights living the way of Korlacchi' who once camped beyond Ragunna.
Land of Xuanfang: The borderland between Jinzhou and Mengzhou, home to Xuanfang Hold, the mechanical city Hsin built to trap Tacet Discords, and the main front of the Fortress and Gorges War two centuries ago.
Laurel: The honour at the height of Ragunna's Carnevale: the Sentinel is said to crown the finest performer, who may then commune with Imperator. A Laurel won by a Montelli ancestor is part of that family's legend.
Liondance: Jinzhou's lion dance, a mix of martial arts and dance that began as a celebration of victories over Tacet Discords. It is performed before soldiers march and at the Spring Loong Festival; Lingyang leads the Liondance Troupe.
Loong: The Huanglong dragon. Jinzhou's Sentinel Jué takes the form of a Loong, which led the people to refuge near Mt. Firmament; it gives its name to the city's lanterns, festivals and landmarks such as Loong's Crest.
Magistrate of Jinzhou: The head of Jinzhou's government, chosen with Sentinel Jué's involvement. The current Magistrate is Jinhsi, the 'Loong Maiden'.
Miko of Flaming Sakura: Ashinohara's miko title, held by Hiyuki, who keeps the Legacy Talisman Suzu. In Ashinohara, Mikos appear only in the darkest of times.
Modulation: The process of adjusting frequencies, a core Black Shores technique; Modulation Devices help safeguard the Tethys System.
Moon-Chasing Festival: One of Huanglong's most important festivals, a night for family reunions and wishes. Its best-known origin story, 'The Fox and the Moon', stars the merrymaking Sentinel Hsin.
Mya: A Septimont gladiator who became a Harbinger of the Dark Tide. Cristoforo used her until the power could be separated from her; she was finally laid to rest when peace returned to Septimont.
Napoli II: The first Primus of the Order of the Deep, who by the Order's account stopped the first Dark Tide. His lantern later awakened Fenrico's resolve to seal it again.
Neon Tower: The tower at the heart of Honami City where the Lament that trapped the city in a Sonoro Sphere began; those caught inside believed the key to breaking its endless loop lay within.
New Solar Ceremony: Lahai-Roi's 'sun-changing' ceremony (换日仪式), tied to the Reactor Drive that lights the underground city. An incident during the celebration is part of the Startorch Academy story.
Outriders: The Midnight Rangers' scouts (踏白), sent ahead to reconnoitre and prepare for what the General plans and the Sentinel foretells. Yangyang is one of them.
Overseer: The rank of the Fractsidus's leading agents, each with a codename, among them Scar, Phrolova (Hecate) and Cristoforo (Arachnos). They answer to the Grand Architect.
Phantoms: Apparitions met in Sonoro Spheres and the Somnoire, echoes of fallen warriors or of memories, often impossible to tell apart from Tacet Discord simulations.
Professor Heisen: The researcher behind the experiments in the controlled Tacet Field of the Chapter I ruins. He removed every clock to keep the field stable, and his recorded words about those who are 'our past and our future' point at Rover.
Resonance Beacons: Infrastructure that stabilises and relays frequencies across a region. Huaxu Academy built Jinzhou's network, and beacon data feeds the Tethys System's warnings.
Resonance Nexus: The central beacon that anchors a region's Resonance Beacons. Rinascita's is the Genesis Nexus, and Huanglong chose Jinzhou as its new capital from Nexus projections.
Rite of Offering: An old Mt. Firmament ritual. Its inscriptions send pilgrims to the glazed lamp on Xuanji Ridge and recall how Jué's time-distorting power once protected the people.
Roya Frostlands: The frozen surface above Lahai-Roi near the north pole, homeland of the Roya before the Lament froze it. Access is restricted; a vertical transport along the Exostrider's greatsword links it to the city below.
Royan Mythology: The Roya Tribe's myths, built on cycles of the old giving way to the new: the lens through which the Roya read themselves and the world.
Secret of Immortality: Mt. Firmament's legend of immortality. The 'secret' is the Temporal Disruptions, which some wrongly hoped could halt ageing.
Subject A038: A specimen in the Chapter I ruins' research records, kept in a 6-metre artificial, controllable Tacet Field.
Séance Society: A Jinzhou group promising contact with lost loved ones, and home of the Dollmaker. Yinlin tried to mediate between it and the Fractsidus, and failed.
TD Outbreaks: Mass surges of Tacet Discords from Tacet Fields that can wipe out whole settlements; outbreaks from the Norfall Barrens led to Huanglong's first frontier fortress.
Tacet Core: The crystal core of a Tacet Discord. Some Resonators carry one: when Calcharo Overclocks, Tacet Discord erosion spreads and the golden Tacet Core on his chest flickers.
The False Sovereign: An autonomous creation of the Dark Tide in Septimont that devours nearby frequencies to grow stronger; Rover and Augusta hunt it down.
The Lost Beyond: Phrolova's Sonoro Sphere, a recreation of Ostina, her birthplace, built in the Fabricatorium of the Deep by merging Reverberations with Tacet Discords.
The Shepherd: One of the three Roya callings, with the Solsworn and the Heliodic Six, rooted in the tribe's nomad past. Scar also blames a mysterious 'Shepherd' for a destruction.
The Truthseeker's Pass: A trial path on Mt. Firmament that Xinyi points Rover to during the search for Sentinel Jué.
Thundering Mephis: A Tidespawn beast not native to Rinascita. Hunting it, Rover learns that Avidius came to Ragunna looking for the Quillbearer.
Wayfinder: A guide into restricted ground. Changli serves as Rover's 'Wayfinder' into Mt. Firmament, and another waits at Whining Aix's Mire.
Windmill Keepers: Nameless knights who settled Whisperwind Haven and became its Windmill Keepers, though, as it turns out, not to protect the windmills.
Abraxas: A name bound to Abby. Leviathan called Abby 'Abraxas' and asked why it had betrayed 'us', hinting at a past tie to the Threnodians; Abby finds the name strangely familiar.
Dreaming Deep: The deepest layer of the Somnoire. The Dreaming Deep event revealed that the Somnoire was originally a single layer.
Goddess: The goddess-like figure from the opening cinematic who sends Rover on their way. Who she is remains one of the game's central open questions.
Tacet Eye: Discussed only in fan theories so far; no in-game definition has been found.
